x: The RBI began work on 1 April 1935 under the RBI Act, 1934. It was nationalised in 1949.
t: Discriminate the Act year, start date and nationalisation year.

x: Option A is incorrect: the RBI was nationalised in 1949, not 1937. Its head office moved from Kolkata to Mumbai in 1937.
t: Discriminate the year the office moved from the year of nationalisation.

x: Both are true: the RBI is the lender of last resort because it gives banks emergency liquidity when no one else will. R explains A.
t: Ask whether the act explains the role.

x: As banker to government it handles transactions and public debt; as controller of credit it runs monetary policy. It also manages forex reserves and oversees payment systems. The answer is a-iv, b-iii, c-i, d-ii.
t: Match each RBI role to its task.

x: A is true and B is false: the Government of India (Ministry of Finance) issues both the ₹1 note and coins. The RBI issues all other notes.
t: Discriminate what the government issues from what the RBI issues.

x: Both are true: RBI stands for Reserve Bank of India, which is India's central bank.
t: Recall the RBI's status.

x: The RBI is a statutory body, set up under the RBI Act, 1934. It is not a commercial bank or a ministry.
t: Discriminate statutory from constitutional bodies.

x: Both are true: the RBI is the bankers' bank because commercial banks keep their deposits and reserves with it. R explains A.
t: Ask whether the practice explains the role.

x: Advising banks is monetary advice, regulating banks is supervision, and the RBI also supports financial and economic development. The answer is a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Match each RBI role to its description.

x: Option D is incorrect: the ₹1 note is issued by the Government of India (Ministry of Finance), not the RBI. The government also issues coins.
t: Discriminate what the government issues from what the RBI issues.

x: The bank rate is the RBI's lending (discount) rate, repo is lending against securities, reverse repo absorbs liquidity, and OMO is buying or selling government securities. The answer is a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.
t: Match each tool to its action.

x: Both are true: CRR is kept as cash with the RBI, and no interest is paid on it. Where it is kept does not explain why it earns nothing, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether a location explains a rule.

x: Option C is incorrect: the ₹1 note is issued by the Government of India through the Ministry of Finance, not by the RBI. The RBI is banker to the Centre and the States and manages public debt.
t: Recall which currency the government, not the RBI, issues.
o: The RBI acts as banker to the Central Government.
The RBI manages government borrowing and public debt.
The RBI issues the ₹1 note on behalf of the Government.
The RBI acts as banker to State Governments.

x: MSF is an emergency overnight borrowing window for banks, at a rate above repo. CRR, SLR and reverse repo are the other options.
t: Match each tool to its action.

x: Both are true: banks hold their SLR themselves, in cash, gold or approved securities and other liquid assets.
t: Discriminate SLR from CRR.

x: CRR is the Cash Reserve Ratio, SLR the Statutory Liquidity Ratio, repo is RBI lending against securities, and MSF the emergency overnight window. The answer is a-ii, b-i, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Match each tool to its meaning.

x: All three are correct: SLR assets such as government bonds earn returns, CRR controls liquidity and credit, and SLR controls liquidity and acts as a buffer.
t: Discriminate SLR from CRR.

x: The RBI advises the government on monetary and financial matters. The 'only' options narrow its role.
t: Watch for 'only' narrowing the role.

x: M3 (broad money) is the most used measure of money supply. M1 is narrow money, and M0 is reserve money.
t: Discriminate M0, M1 and M3.

x: Option C is incorrect: time deposits are not part of M1 but are part of M3. M1 is currency, demand deposits and other RBI deposits.
t: Use M3 = M1 + time deposits.

x: Both are true: a lower bank rate is expansionary because it makes borrowing cheaper and adds liquidity. R explains A.
t: Follow cheaper credit to more liquidity.

x: Currency is cash in hand, demand deposits can be withdrawn at once, time deposits are locked for a fixed term and least liquid, and other deposits with the RBI are balances of foreign central banks and international bodies. The answer is a-iii, b-ii, c-i, d-iv.
t: Rank each item by liquidity.
s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Currency with the public
(b) Demand deposits with banks
(c) Time deposits with banks
(d) Other deposits with RBI

List-II
i. Locked for a fixed period; least liquid
ii. Instant withdrawal on demand from a bank account
iii. Immediate cash in hand
iv. Balances of foreign central banks and international bodies held with the RBI

x: I, II and IV are correct: the money multiplier is M3 divided by M0, and more banking habit raises it. III is false because a higher CRR reduces credit creation.
t: Follow how CRR affects credit.

x: All four are correct: M1 is narrow money, includes demand deposits, is highly liquid, and can be spent directly.
t: Recall the features of M1.

x: Both are true: M3 is M1 plus time deposits with banks, so M3 minus M1 is time deposits.
t: Use M3 = M1 + time deposits.

x: Both are true: withdrawing ₹1 lakh cuts demand deposits and raises currency with the public by the same amount, so total money supply stays the same. R explains A.
t: Check that both parts are inside M1.

x: Policy rates directly control how much credit banks can create. The other options are definitions of money measures.
t: Recall what policy rates act on.

x: Both are true: currency with the public and demand deposits are in M1, and so also in M3.
t: Use M3 = M1 + time deposits.

x: The repo rate is the rate at which the RBI lends to banks against securities, to add liquidity. Reverse repo is the RBI borrowing from banks.
t: Discriminate repo from reverse repo.

x: Option C is incorrect: under reverse repo the RBI borrows from banks to soak up surplus liquidity. Banks borrowing from the RBI is repo.
t: Discriminate repo from reverse repo.

x: Both are true: repo manages liquidity because through it the RBI lends to banks against eligible securities, adding money as needed. R explains A.
t: Ask whether the method explains the use.

x: Under repo the RBI lends short-term against securities, under reverse repo it absorbs surplus liquidity, the bank rate is its long-term rediscount rate on bills, and the fiscal deficit measures government borrowing under fiscal policy. The answer is a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Separate the three monetary tools by direction and term, and set the fiscal measure apart.
s:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) Repo Rate
(b) Reverse Repo Rate
(c) Bank Rate
(d) Fiscal deficit

List-II
(i) Fiscal policy indicator of government borrowing
(ii) RBI lends short-term to banks against government securities
(iii) RBI absorbs surplus liquidity from banks
(iv) RBI rediscounts bills of exchange over the long term

x: I and II are correct: the bank rate is the RBI's long-term rediscount rate on bills of exchange and commercial paper. III is false because absorbing surplus liquidity is the reverse repo.
t: Match each tool to its action.

x: Option A is incorrect: under repo the RBI lends to banks for short periods. The RBI borrowing from banks is reverse repo. CRR and SLR are monetary tools.
t: Discriminate repo from reverse repo.

x: Under CRR, banks keep cash with the RBI. SLR assets (cash, gold, government securities) are kept by the bank itself.
t: Discriminate CRR from SLR.

x: Option C is incorrect: SLR is held by the bank itself in liquid assets. Cash deposited with the RBI is CRR.
t: Discriminate CRR from SLR.

x: Both are true: a higher SLR leaves banks less to lend because more of their funds are locked in liquid assets. R explains A.
t: Follow higher SLR to less lending.

x: SLR is held by the bank itself and CRR with the RBI; raising SLR cuts loanable funds and lowering it frees them. The answer is a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii.
t: Discriminate CRR from SLR.

x: All three are correct: raising SLR is a contractionary credit control that cuts credit and money supply, and is used against inflation.
t: Follow higher SLR to less money supply.
s:
Consider the following statements:
I. Raising the SLR acts as a contractionary quantitative credit control tool.
II. An increase in SLR can reduce credit creation and contract money supply.
III. Raising the SLR is used during inflation to rein in excessive commercial bank credit growth.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: Both are true: a lower SLR boosts economic activity because banks hold less in mandatory assets and can lend more. R explains A.
t: Follow lower SLR to more lending.

x: Option C is incorrect: MSF costs more than repo, usually repo plus 0.25%. It is an overnight emergency window, while repo is for regular liquidity.
t: Recall that MSF costs more than repo.

x: A is true and B is false: repo is the main policy lending rate and the tool for regular liquidity. MSF is for emergency, marginal needs.
t: Discriminate regular from emergency borrowing.
s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Repo is the RBI's principal policy lending rate.
Statement B: MSF is used for regular liquidity management.
o: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true

x: MSF is overnight emergency borrowing above the repo rate that lets banks dip into SLR, repo is the main policy rate for regular liquidity, the Standing Deposit Facility absorbs surplus liquidity without collateral, and the bank rate is the rediscount rate on bills. The answer is a-ii, b-i, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Separate injection tools from absorption tools, and emergency from regular windows.
s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Marginal Standing Facility
(b) Repo
(c) Standing Deposit Facility
(d) Bank Rate

List-II
(i) Principal policy rate for regular liquidity management
(ii) Overnight emergency borrowing above the repo rate, allowing banks to dip into SLR
(iii) Absorbs surplus liquidity from banks without collateral
(iv) Rate at which the RBI rediscounts bills of exchange

x: All three are correct: repo is short-term borrowing by banks from the RBI against eligible securities.
t: Recall the features of repo.
